decisions.decision: One Payment Record or Customer Credit is allocated to one or more Invoice receivables in a single backend ledger transaction. Backend owns buyer/currency/outstanding/residual checks, allocation IDs, time, audit and events.
Reversal is an immutable ledger command over one effective allocation; backend restores source residual and emits reversal evidence.
Public API creates an asynchronous Refund Intent only. Provider execution and SUCCEEDED/FAILED completion, refund Payment Record and timestamps are backend-owned.
Customer collection evidence is distinct from merchant remittance and never makes COD effective for receivables.
Merchant remittance requires customer collection; only REMITTED makes the COD Payment effective for receivables.

decisions.question: How does Return approval release allocations, create credits/refund intents and settle Invoice/Receivable state atomically or as a saga?
decisions.reason: Cross-module compensation, retry and partial-failure semantics remain incomplete.

decisions.question: When may a failed/processing refund be cancelled or retried and how is provider idempotency retained?
decisions.reason: Frontend only proves creation and backend completion/failure primitives.
